This page documents a [[id:31C868B9-306E-4282-BA8C-07E647021B34][task]] in the [[id:09FA0936-289A-4016-A0A2-88C0A5F05870][Harden the gates the component clean standard rests on]] story. It captures the goal, current status, acceptance, and any notes or results.

* Goal

Widen the drift gate so it covers generated output that no run of a component's
own models can reach.

The gate's coverage is the registry, and the registry lists the components that
are already clean. Two holes follow. An archetype can route a model's output
into another component's tree, so no run of either component reaches it. And the
catalogue holds components the registry does not list, so their generated output
has no gate at all.

* Acceptance

- A sweep renders every catalogue component, not the registry, so output an
  archetype routes into another component's tree is reached.
- It fails only on files the branch touched, because a component's remaining
  drift belongs to that component's own clean-up story.
- It renders into a temporary root and writes nothing, so it is safe on a branch
  whose templates are older than main's.
- It refuses when the commit to compare against cannot be resolved, rather than
  treating every component's clean-up debt as a failure.
- It fails when the catalogue yields no component to render, rather than passing
  a tree it read nothing from.
- A file the branch deleted whose model still produces it fails, as a
  would-create. A committed deletion of a path no model produces any more is out
  of scope, and the limit is recorded.

* Plan

*Two holes, one cause.* =check_component_drift.py --all= renders the components
in =COMPONENTS_UNDER_TEST= and compares the tree. That set is ten components. The
catalogue holds twenty-four entries, which name twenty-one distinct modeling
directories, because =trade= and =trading-cpp=, =dq= and =dq-cpp=, and =iam= and
=iam-cpp= are second spellings of one component each; one of the twenty-one,
=controller-cpp=, has no models and no modeling directory in the tree, so twenty
components render. So a component waiting its turn has no gate, and neither does
output an archetype routes into another component's tree.

*Measured, for hole A.* The shell-command facet's output pattern routes by the
*model's* component rather than by the catalogue component a run names, so
rendering =ores.trading= at the =ores.cpp= address writes 66 files under
=projects/ores.shell/trading/=. Rendering =ores.shell= cannot reach them, because
shell owns one model and it produces the composite root. The directory holds 76
files in total: the 66 the trade render produces, nine CMake, diagram and
documentation files, and one further source file.

*Measured, for hole B.* The =ores.service= clean-up moved three workflow header
names out of =ores.service= into =ores.workflow.api=, and =ores.refdata= keeps a
workflow override as a source block pasted into a generated handler. The
generated file was hand-edited and the model left naming the deleted symbols.
=check_component_drift.py --all= was green and CI was green on every head,
because refdata is not in the registry.

*The rule, and why it needs a base.* A full comparison cannot be the rule: 645
files would change across the catalogue today, and that debt belongs to each
component's own clean-up. So the sweep fails only on a path it would change that
the branch also touched. That needs the commit the branch diverged from, so the
sweep takes the merge base with =origin/main= and refuses when it cannot resolve
one. A wrong answer there is silent, which is worse than a refusal.

*Why a render and not a symbol check.* The capture proposed a cheaper half as
well: a check that every symbol a model's pasted block names resolves in the
tree. That is a different guarantee and it is not in this task. It would catch a
model and its generated file that agree with each other and are both stale,
which the sweep cannot see because the render reproduces the committed bytes.
The sweep catches the disagreement, which is the measured case.

*Cost.* A full sweep renders twenty components and takes about a minute: 74
seconds measured here and 61 on the reviewing machine, so the figure moves with
the hardware. The workflow job is 2 minutes with its setup. That is why it is its
own workflow rather than another step in =codegen-drift.yml=. That workflow fires
on the inputs codegen reads; the sweep exists for the output codegen writes, and
the measured case touched no model at all, so it fires on any change under
=projects/=.

*Two limits this sweep does not close.* Both are the price of rendering per
technical space rather than at the whole =ores= address, and neither is covered
by a test.

- *Generated recipes are not reached.* The recipe facets declare
  =#+requires_facet:= on a facet in another technical space, so they fire only at
  the whole =ores= address. Measured for =ores.trading=, whose 64 models make the
  two paths comparable: rendering each model at the whole =ores= address gives
  2,003 files, 22 of them recipes; the sweep's own path, which expands =ores= into
  the technical spaces, gives 1,867 files and no recipe at all. The two calls are
  easy to confuse, because passing =ores= to =_render_components= expands it
  rather than rendering it, so a measurement of the whole address has to go
  through =_generate_single=. The 247 files at the generated recipe path shape
  under =doc/recipes/shell/= and =doc/recipes/http= -- 233 and 14, of which 172
  carry the =:tangle= block a generated recipe exports -- therefore have no gate,
  and a branch that deletes one cannot be caught either.
- *A generated file no render produces is invisible.* The comparison walks the
  render's output, so a tree file the models do not produce is never examined.
  That is what keeps each component's 645 files of clean-up debt out of the
  result, but it also means the sweep cannot report a file that should exist and
  does not, once its model no longer produces it. A file the branch deleted whose
  model still produces it *is* caught, as a would-create; the deletion is caught
  only while some model still produces the path. A committed deletion of a path
  no model produces any more -- the shape a retired, renamed or moved template
  leaves behind, and so the shape a cross-component rename leaves behind -- is
  silent.

* Result

=check_component_drift.py --sweep= renders every catalogue component that owns a
modeling directory, twenty of them, into a temporary root and compares the result
against the repository. It reaches the two kinds of generated output the registry
cannot: a component waiting its turn, and output an archetype routes into another
component's tree. Rendering =ores.trading= at the =ores.cpp= address writes 66
files under =projects/ores.shell/trading/=, and no run of =ores.shell= can reach
them.

It fails only on a path it would change that the branch also touched, because 645
files would change across the catalogue today and that debt belongs to each
component's own clean-up. The base is the merge base with =origin/main=, and the
sweep refuses when it cannot resolve one rather than reading every component's
debt as a failure. It renders and compares only, so it writes nothing and is safe
on a branch whose templates are older than main's.

It runs in its own workflow, =codegen-sweep.yml=, which fires on any change under
=projects/= because the measured case touched no model at all. A full sweep takes
about a minute, 74 seconds measured here and 61 on the reviewing machine, and the
job is 2 minutes with its setup. It is named in V05 of the Component Clean
Standard and in the =compass-pr-raise= gate roster. Thirteen tests drive the rule
against a throw-away tree with the render stubbed, and the codegen suite is 887
passed.

Two limits are recorded rather than closed, and both are the price of rendering
per technical space: the recipe facets fire only at the whole =ores= address, so
the 247 files at the generated recipe path shape have no gate; and the comparison
walks the render's output, so a committed deletion of a path no model produces any
more is silent.
